subject: Best way to get nimbleModel() to not print warnings?

messages.author: 63cc02caac0434cf
messages.subject: Best way to get nimbleModel() to not print warnings?
parts:
Hi,

I am running some simulations and because I am simulating some variables I do not fully initialize the model. As a result when running nimbleModel() I get an extremely long list of warnings (likely thousands of pages worth). Is there some way to get nimbleModel() to not print the warnings? 

Thanks!
Dirk

messages.author: 9b1f1220a2b07d1e
messages.subject: Re: Best way to get nimbleModel() to not print warnings?
parts:
Hi Dirk--

There might also be a built-in way to do this but you can do

suppressMessages(mod <- nimbleModel(...))

Ben

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Best way to get nimbleModel() to not print warnings?
parts:
Hi Dirk,

Those messages (if it's the step I'm thinking) are from pure R evaluation, when the uncompiled model is calculated by nimbleModel after being set up for the first time.

The argument calculate=FALSE to nimbleModel will make it not do that step.  Just be aware that after compiling the model, you might want to do Cmodel$calculate() to get everything calculated.  It really depends on what you are doing to do with the model.

Also according to help(options), if you set options(warn = -1), or any negative value, all warnings will be ignored by R.

Do either of those make your workflow more reasonable?

Perry

messages.author: d78486bfff620d81
messages.subject: Re: Best way to get nimbleModel() to not print warnings?
parts:
Hi Dirk,

Yeah, we don't have a way of suppressing the dynamic index out of bounds warnings, in part because those are printed out either in compiled or uncompiled execution of model calculations.

It's fine to not run calculate() as long as you ensure that in your simulate() calls you are using the correct values of  all the deterministic nodes that are parents of stochastic nodes you are simulating.

E.g. in the model below, if you simulate theta, you'd then need to simulate (or calculate as the two are equivalent for a deterministic node) z before simulating y. In general of course you should use getDependencies and similar model API calls to determine the relevant nodes (since nimble introduces hidden lifted nodes in a number of situations).

theta ~ dnorm(0,1)
z <- theta + 2
y ~ dnorm(z, 1)

-chris

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Best way to get nimbleModel() to not print warnings?
parts:
Hi Dirk,

You get a prize for a collection of wrong answers (including mine) before the right answer to your question appeared from Chris.

On the topic calculate and simulate, here is an example.  If your model code included:

a ~ dnorm(0, 1)
b <- 2*a
c ~ (a, 1)

Say you do not initialize a or c.  When you build the model (nimbleModel step), you get told some nodes are not initialized.  (In your actual case, lack of initialization also leads to warnings due to how the nodes are used in dependent calculations.)

If you then do:

model$a <- 1
model$simulate('c')

you would get nonsense (or an error) in c because b was never calculated.  If instead you do:

model$simulate(c('b', 'c'))

then it would work fine.  The definition of simulate for a deterministic node is the same as calculate: just do the calculation.

The model-generic way to do this would be:

model$simulate( model$getDependencies("a", self=FALSE))

That is also safer in case there are any lifted nodes in the model (see User Manual).

(In all of this, 'model' could be the uncompiled or the compiled model.)

If you are simulating everything, i.e. model$simulate(), then these issues are moot anyway and it should work.

I hope that helps.

Perry
